records.quote: The most merciful thing in the world, I think, is the inability of the human mind to correlate all its contents. We live on a placid island of ignorance in the midst of black seas of infinity, and it was not meant that we should voyage far. The sciences, each straining in its own direction, have hitherto harmed us little; but some day the piecing together of dissociated knowledge will open up such terrifying vistas of reality
records.paraphrase: The narrator explains a premise that piecing together separated pieces of scientific knowledge will reveal terrifying realities.

records.quote: There then followed an exhaustive comparison of details, and a moment of really awed silence when both detective and scientist agreed on the virtual identity of the phrase common to two hellish rituals so many worlds of distance apart.
records.paraphrase: The detective and scientist systematically compare ritual phrases and find them identical across distant cultures.

records.quote: What has risen may sink, and what has sunk may rise. Loathsomeness waits and dreams in the deep, and decay spreads over the tottering cities of men. A time will come
records.paraphrase: The narrator projects an inevitable future return of Cthulhu and decline of human civilization.

records.quote: twisted menace and suspense lurked leeringly in those crazily elusive angles of carven rock where a second glance showed concavity after the first showed convexity
records.paraphrase: The rock's angles behave contrary to ordinary spatial expectation, shifting between concave and convex.

records.quote: The time would be easy to know, for then mankind would have become as the Great Old Ones; free and wild and beyond good and evil, with laws and morals thrown aside and all men shouting and killing and reveling in joy.
records.paraphrase: A projected future in which humanity, upon the Old Ones' return, abandons all morality in violent ecstasy.

records.quote: After vigintillions of years great Cthulhu was loose again, and ravening for delight.
records.paraphrase: The long-dormant entity Cthulhu is released into the world.

records.quote: They all lay in stone houses in Their great city of R'lyeh, preserved by the spells of mighty Cthulhu for a glorious resurrection when the stars and the earth might once more be ready for Them.
records.paraphrase: The Old Ones lie preserved across vast time in R'lyeh awaiting a future resurrection.

records.quote: My uncle, it seems, had quickly instituted a prodigiously far-flung body of inquiries amongst nearly all the friends whom he could question without impertinence, asking for nightly reports of their dreams, and the dates of any notable visions for some time past.
records.paraphrase: The professor conducts a wide survey collecting people's dream reports and dates.

records.quote: The great stone city R'lyeh, with its monoliths and sepulchers, had sunk beneath the waves; and the deep waters, full of the one primal mystery through which not even thought can pass, had cut off the spectral intercourse.
records.paraphrase: In the past the city R'lyeh sank beneath the sea, severing dream contact.

records.quote: the soapy, greenish-black stone with its golden or iridescent flecks and striations resembled nothing familiar to geology or mineralogy
records.paraphrase: The statuette's stone material is described as matching nothing known to geology or mineralogy.

records.quote: He had said that the geometry of the dream-place he saw was abnormal, non-Euclidean, and loathsomely redolent of spheres and dimensions apart from ours.
records.paraphrase: The city's geometry is described as non-Euclidean and belonging to dimensions apart from ours.

records.quote: Now an unlettered seaman felt the same thing whilst gazing at the terrible reality.
records.paraphrase: An uneducated sailor independently perceives the same abnormal geometry described by the sculptor, corroborating its reality.

records.quote: He questioned the sculptor with scientific minuteness; and studied with almost frantic intensity the bas-relief on which the youth had found himself working
records.paraphrase: Professor Angell interrogates the sculptor methodically and studies the artifact intensively.

records.quote: I have looked upon all that the universe has to hold of horror, and even the skies of spring and the flowers of summer must ever afterward be poison to me.
records.paraphrase: The narrator reports that his knowledge has permanently poisoned his perception of the world.

records.quote: They worshiped, so they said, the Great Old Ones who lived ages before there were any men, and who came to the young world out of the sky. Those Old Ones were gone now, inside the earth and under the sea; but their dead bodies had told their secrets in dreams to the first man, who formed a cult which had never died.
records.paraphrase: The cult's account explains the Great Old Ones as beings who came from the sky before humanity and communicate through dreams.

records.quote: what an age-old cult had failed to do by design, a band of innocent sailors had done by accident. After vigintillions of years great Cthulhu was loose again
records.paraphrase: The accidental awakening of Cthulhu represents a potential worldwide catastrophe.

records.quote: Briden looked back and went mad, laughing shrilly as he kept on laughing at intervals till death found him one night in the cabin whilst Johansen was wandering deliriously.
records.paraphrase: A crew member goes insane and laughs until death after witnessing Cthulhu.

candidate.quote: These Great Old Ones, Castro continued, were not composed altogether of flesh and blood. They had shape/u2014for did not this star-fashioned image prove it?/u2014but that shape was not made of matter. When the stars were right, They could plunge from world to world through the sky; but when the stars were wrong, They could not live.
candidate.paraphrase: Castro explains the physical nature of the Old Ones and how their viability depends on stellar alignment.

criteria.rationale: The story invokes scientific framing (geology, mineralogy, non-Euclidean geometry, the premise of correlating dissociated knowledge), but these serve as gestures toward the unknowable rather than materially represented science; the entities are supernatural/cosmic rather than genuinely scientific phenomena.

No engineered device, technique, or invention materially drives the setting, problem, or outcome. The bas-relief and idol are artifacts of cult/ancient origin, not inventions; ordinary boats and brass cannon are incidental contemporary tools.

The story centrally invokes a remote past (vigintillions of years, eons before mankind, star-born Old Ones preserved across vast time) and projects a future return, materially anchoring the narrative in deep temporal scale.

The narrator develops consequences from an identifiable premise (correlating dissociated knowledge; the Old Ones' cyclical return) into projected outcomes: humanity's descent into amoral frenzy and the decay of civilization upon Cthulhu's return.

Professor Angell and the narrator systematically gather dream reports with dates, compare ritual phrases across cultures, correlate press cuttings, and build inference from evidence; this investigative, evidence-correlating method materially drives the growing understanding of the Cthulhu cult.

The Great Old Ones are visitors who came to earth from the stars, and R'lyeh is a substantially nonordinary environment with non-Euclidean geometry and dimensions apart from ours; these cosmic visitors and their alien locus are central to the story.

The accidental awakening of Cthulhu represents an impending world-scale catastrophe: the entity is loose and ravening, mass insanity and civilizational decline are projected, forming a causally central cosmic disaster narrowly averted by R'lyeh's re-sinking.

candidates.description: The Great Old Ones, chiefly Cthulhu: vast extraterrestrial beings who came from the stars in remote prehuman eons, lie in death-like suspension in the sunken city R'lyeh, communicate with sensitive humans through molded dreams, and await a cosmic-cyclical resurrection when 'the stars are right' that will overturn human civilization.

novelty.rationale: The Old Ones constitute a totalizing difference from the empirical norm: prehuman star-born entities who ruled earth, whose existence and looming return relegate humanity to a 'transient incident' and reveal the cosmos as fundamentally other than the reader's world. The corroborated identity of rituals across Greenland, Louisiana, and China establishes this as a world-scale reality rather than a local marvel.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The account is systematic, immanent, and explicitly nonsupernatural in framing: the beings 'came to the young world out of the sky,' are made of a shape that is not ordinary matter, obey a determinate stellar/cosmic cycle, communicate via transmitted thought, and are investigated through empirical inquiry (dream surveys, comparative ritual philology, geology, mineralogy). The story develops a coherent imaginary science of materialist cosmic horror; scientific method is a persistent structuring device.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The Old Ones govern the entire narrative logic. The framing (correlating dissociated knowledge into terrifying reality), the three-part investigative structure (bas-relief, Legrasse's cult, Johansen's voyage), the accidental awakening of Cthulhu, and the closing projection of humanity's doom all derive from and serve this novum. It is not an incidental device but the determining premise.

estrangement.rationale: Estrangement operates through the contrast between the reader's anthropocentric, rationalist empirical norm and the corroborated revelation of prehuman cosmic masters. The non-Euclidean architecture perceived identically by an educated sculptor and an unlettered seaman, the geologically impossible stone, and the globally synchronized cult rituals present the strange as objectively real, poisoning the narrator's perception of ordinary skies and flowers.
